key_points: Indian C&W industry projected to grow at 12% CAGR to Rs1.7tr by FY30F, driven by concurrent demand super-cycles across five sectors
Cable-heavy players structurally superior with high entry barriers, government anchor-buyer dynamics, and superior margins vs wire-focused peers
NEP 2022-32 mandates 191,474ckm transmission lines with 14-15% cable content implying Rs1.28-1.37tr cable demand from T&D alone
EHV segment dominated by few certified domestic players; moving up voltage ladder increases both margins and barriers to entry
DIACABS positioned with India's largest single-location backward-integrated facility, underutilised capacity can scale topline >5x at minimal capex
Organised market share to increase from 76% (FY25) to 84% (FY30F) as unorganised players face certification and capability hurdles
Multiple concurrent demand drivers reduce single-sector slowdown risk: T&D, renewables, data centres, EVs, real estate all spending simultaneously
Exports gaining momentum with specialty cables and higher-voltage products commanding premiums in developed markets
catalysts: India's 500GW renewable energy target capacity additions
Data centre capex from Google, AWS hyperscaler commitments (8,327MW pipeline)
EV charging network rollout and electric vehicle adoption curve
RDSS (Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme) grid modernisation execution
Real estate activity and smart city electrification projects
Underground cable conversion mandates in urban areas
Export market share gains in developed economies
reports.summary: India's cables & wires industry is entering a multi-year super-cycle anchored in government-mandated infrastructure spending, with projected 12% CAGR growth to Rs1.7tr by FY30F. Cable-focused players with EHV capabilities enjoy structural advantages through high entry barriers, superior margins, and government procurement visibility. DIACABS emerges as the highest-conviction opportunity given its backward-integrated capacity and significant upside potential, while Finolex Cables offers complementary exposure to the secular electrification theme.
reports.connection_narrative: India's cables and wires sector is entering a transformational phase driven by five concurrent and non-correlated demand super-cycles that are structurally reshaping the country's energy and digital infrastructure. The National Electricity Plan 2022-32 mandates 191,474 circuit kilometers of new transmission lines and a doubling of sub-station capacity by fiscal 2032, representing the single largest government-anchored infrastructure commitment in Indian power history. Simultaneously, India's commitment to 500 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity by 2030 requires massive cable investments for evacuation infrastructure, while the emerging hyperscaler data centre ecosystem backed by commitments from Google and AWS is creating a new demand vector for high-specification cables in the 8,327-megawatt pipeline. The electric vehicle charging network rollout and the ongoing real estate formalization through compliance-driven premiumization towards fire-retardant specifications add further structural tailwinds. These parallel investment cycles mean that the sector's growth is no longer dependent on a single cyclical driver, providing unprecedented demand visibility for cable manufacturers with the certifications and scale to serve government and utility-grade projects. Cable-focused companies structurally outperform their wire-centric peers because the cable market commands 66 percent of industry value, operates with higher entry barriers requiring years of regulatory certification and specialized manufacturing capabilities, enjoys government as the anchor buyer providing visibility and payment security, and benefits from margin expansion as infrastructure moves up the voltage ladder from low-voltage to medium, high, and extra-high voltage segments where certified players are severely limited. Diamond Power Infrastructure emerges as the highest-conviction opportunity through its ownership of India's largest single-location backward-integrated cable and conductor manufacturing complex, which remains significantly underutilized in a supply-constrained market and possesses the technical capability to scale revenue more than five-fold at minimal incremental capex, essentially positioning the company as a new, fully-equipped competitor entering an industry starved for capacity. Finolex Cables and KEI Industries already possess extra-high voltage capabilities and stand to benefit from the premiumization trend, while Polycab India's impending EHV capacity commissioning in the third quarter of fiscal 2027 should unlock meaningful growth contribution thereafter, though current valuations offer limited upside from present levels. The most critical near-term catalyst to monitor is the pace of transmission line execution under the National Electricity Plan, as any slowdown would constrain cable offtake volumes across the entire industry, while the primary downside risk remains the potential emergence of new entrants with sufficient capital and government support to disrupt pricing dynamics or the possibility of extended bottlenecks in mega-infrastructure projects causing demand pushouts beyond current visibility windows.

key_points: India's only vertically integrated precision aerospace manufacturer with NADCAP-certified capabilities
Consolidated revenue/EBITDA poised to grow 7x/17x by FY31 as Consumer Electronics turns profitable
Global aerospace supply gap of 23-43% over CY22-25 creating structural pricing power and order visibility
Consumer Electronics TAM expansion 10x to US$130bn with breakthrough entry in 2025 serving anchor customer
Target steady-state RoCE of ~20% by FY31 with net margins expanding to 7.4%
Deep competitive moats: high capital intensity, multi-year qualification cycles, stringent certifications, entrenched OEM relationships
Airbus and its OEMs contribute >60% of sales; expanding wallet share into aero-engines and landing gears
catalysts: Consumer Electronics mass commercial production ramp-up and profitability inflection
Aero Engine Ecosystem MoU execution at Hosur, Tamil Nadu
Expansion into higher-value aero-engine and landing gear components
PLI scheme utilization under ECMS for consumer electronics manufacturing
New customer additions (Mattel in toys; major CE anchor customer supply scaling)
Capacity utilization improvement at France and Texas facilities
Global aerospace production rate acceleration as supply constraints persist
reports.summary: Aequs is India's only vertically integrated precision aerospace manufacturer, uniquely positioned to capture structural supply-chain diversification tailwinds from global OEMs amid persistent aerospace supply gaps. The company is simultaneously scaling a high-growth Consumer Electronics business targeting 10x TAM expansion, with consolidated revenue and EBITDA expected to grow 7x and 17x respectively by FY31, driving net margins to 7.4% and steady-state RoCE to 20%.
reports.connection_narrative: India's aerospace manufacturing sector is experiencing a structural inflection driven by multiple converging factors: first, global commercial aircraft demand has rebounded sharply to 2,300 aircraft annually post-COVID while supply remains capped at only 1,250 units, creating a persistent 23-43% supply deficit that will take twelve years to clear at current production rates; second, Western supply chains are actively de-risking from China due to geopolitical tensions, with India emerging as a preferred alternative manufacturing hub combining cost advantage, precision engineering expertise, and proximity to growing domestic demand; third, India's share of the global US$395 billion aerospace manufacturing market is targeted to expand from 2% to 10% over the next decade, representing a structural upside cycle. Within this favorable macro backdrop, Aequs benefits as the only domestic manufacturer with end-to-end vertically integrated capabilities—including precision machining, forging, NADCAP-certified surface treatment, and assembly—all within a single SEZ in Belagavi, creating insurmountable competitive barriers through decades of accumulated process engineering expertise and entrenched relationships with Tier-1 OEMs like Airbus, Boeing, Safran, and Collins Aerospace. The company is simultaneously executing a transformational strategy into high-volume Consumer Electronics, having achieved a breakthrough entry in 2025 serving a major global anchor customer with mechanical components including laptop enclosures and smartwatch casings, expanding its TAM ten-fold to US$130bn; leveraging its precision manufacturing playbook and receiving PLI approval under the ECMS scheme, the Consumer Electronics business is targeted to reach Rs28 billion in revenue within five years at 15-17% operating margins, ultimately driving consolidated EBITDA to grow seventeen times by FY31. The most critical near-term catalyst is the profitability inflection of the Consumer Electronics segment, which currently operates at negative EBITDA but is positioned to turn substantially positive as production scales and volumes increase, with this transition alone capable of rerating the stock significantly. However, the primary risk to monitor is the execution risk on the Consumer Electronics scaling trajectory—if the anchor customer fails to ramp volumes as expected or if new customer wins do not materialize at planned rates, the company's consolidated margin expansion thesis could be materially impaired, particularly given the currently elevated valuation at 197x FY26 EV/EBITDA that relies heavily on achieving these future growth milestones.
